title: Kanhangad-Kaniyur rail line that could halve Bengaluru travel time back on agenda; DK seeks meeting of MLAs, MPs
content: Kasaragod: Efforts to revive the proposed Kanhangad-Kaniyur railway line, which promises to halve travel time between North Malabar and Bengaluru, have gained fresh momentum, with the Kerala Rail Development Corporation Limited (K-Rail) confirming that the state government has again approached the Centre to reconsider the project. The 91-km railway line project was put on the back burner in 2020 amid concerns over its traffic potential and Karnataka's lack of interest. Around 56 per cent of the proposed line from Kanhangad to Panathur (51km) lies in Kasaragod district of Kerala and the rest in Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka. In a letter dated November 10, the K-Rail Managing Director informed Basheer Vellikkoth, convener of the UDF's Kanhangad constituency committee, that the state government had included the project in a memorandum submitted to Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, seeking its revival. The letter was in response to a representation submitted by Vellikkoth and other UDF leaders to Chief Minister V D Satheesan on October 31, seeking urgent intervention to realise the railway line. To be sure, the then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan asked the Railway Ministry to initiate steps to re-sanction the project on a cost-sharing basis. Kerala had conveyed its readiness in 2018 to share 50 per cent of the project cost for the portion falling within its territory. But Karnataka was not enthusiastic. In 2022, the then chief minister Basavaraj Bommai of the BJP rejected the proposal, saying the line would pass through "the rich biodiversity and ecologically sensitive areas of the Western Ghats". Bommai told this to reporters after Vijayan met him in September 2022. But according to Vaishnaw's replies to Unnithan in the Lok Sabha, the Railway Board had shelved the proposal over low traffic projection. When contacted, Unnithan said he believed that the lack of cooperation from Karnataka remained the real obstacle to the project. The MP said he had taken up the proposal with Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar. "He suggested convening a meeting of MPs and MLAs representing the regions through which the proposed railway line would pass," Unnithan said. "So there is a small change in Karnataka's position after the Congress came to power. But as the line originates in Kanhangad and much of the line passes through Kasaragod district, the Kerala government must take the initiative to convene that meeting," he said. Karnataka's objections To be sure, the Bommai government took the position that the proposed line is not beneficial to Karnataka and refused to extend cooperation to the project. He had also cited ecological concerns for rejecting the proposal. Bommai had also opposed the proposed Thalassery-Mysuru railway line on ecological grounds, making his government's position clear at a meeting with Vijayan in September 2022. However, despite being specifically asked by Kasaragod MP Unnithan, the Union government did not cite ecological concerns as a reason for shelving the Kanhangad-Kaniyur project. On December 14, 2022, in a reply to Unnithan's questions on the project, Vaishnaw told the Lok Sabha that the survey for the 90.5 km Kanhangad-Kaniyur line via Panathur had been completed in 2020. Kerala had given its consent to share only 50 per cent of the land acquisition cost for the portion falling within the state, the minister said. "The survey report has been considered. However, the project could not be taken forward due to low traffic potential," Vaishnaw said. When Unnithan raised the issue again, the Railway Minister reiterated the position in a reply on July 31, 2024. Vaishnaw also pointed out that while Kerala had agreed to share the project cost, Karnataka had not given its consent to do so.
